plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-babel **让 DSH 直接使用其他 AI 编码工具生态里的 MCP 服务器、插件与斜杠命令。** > 读它们已有的配置，而不是要求插件作者为 DSH 重新移植一遍。 [![简体中文](https://img.shields.io/badge/lang-%E7%AE%80%E4%BD%93%E4%B8%AD%E6%96%87-red.svg)](README.md) [![English](https://img.shields.io/badge/lang-English-blue.svg)](README.en.md) [![test](https://github.com/Oliveryfaso/dsh-babel/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Oliveryfaso/dsh-babel/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-2EA44F?style=flat)](LICENSE) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/Oliveryfaso/dsh-babel?style=flat&label=%E2%98%85)](https://github.com/Oliveryfaso/dsh-babel) [![DSH plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-plugin-0f766e.svg)](https://github.com/Oliveryfaso/dsh-babel) [![dsh-plugin topic](https://img.shields.io/badge/topic-dsh--plugin-2563eb.svg)](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin)
> dsh-babel 是社区维护的 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）插件，并非 DeepSeek AI 官方产品。 ## 它解决什么问题 插件作者要支持一个平台，就得为它单独写一份目录。一个典型的多平台插件会带六到八个这样的目录： ``` .claude-plugin .codex-plugin .cursor .gemini-extension.json ... ``` DSH 的那个格子通常是空的。dsh-babel 换个思路：**作者不用动，DSH 这边读他们已有的 `.mcp.json` / `commands/`**，把 N×M 的移植问题变成 N×1。 同时它做一件别家没做的事：**装之前就告诉你哪个能跑、哪个缺密钥、哪个根本跑不起来**——而不是装上去之后静默失败。 ## 功能 - **发现**：扫描 Claude Code 与 Codex 插件目录下的 `.mcp.json`，以及两种斜杠命令文件（`.md` / `.toml`）；根目录可配置。 - **归一化**：把多种 `.mcp.json` 方言（带 `mcpServers` 包装的 / 裸顶层的 / Codex 专有键的）降成**一套中间表示**。 - **预检**：四类检查把"静默失败"变成"明确原因"——依赖命令是否在 `PATH`、守护进程是否在跑（如 Docker socket）、密钥是否可用、版本是否未固定。 - **兼容性报告**：把每个服务器归入「可用 / 需密钥 / 不可用」，每条都附具体原因。 - **命令注册**：把发现到的斜杠命令注册进 DSH，支持 `{{args}}` / `$ARGUMENTS` / `$1` 参数替换。 - **MCP 注册**：连上 stdio 或 streamable-http 服务器，用 DSH 自己的 `createMcpToolDefinition` 注册工具。 - **密钥解析**：`process.env` 优先，其次 macOS 钥匙串的**白名单**（仅 GitHub token 家族）——绝不无差别翻钥匙串。 - **展示元数据**：`locale/` 文案与图标，配置项由 schemastery schema 声明，设置界面可渲染。 ## 安装 ```bash # 从 GitHub plugin_manager install_bundle github:Oliveryfaso/dsh-babel # 或本地目录 plugin_manager install_bundle /绝对/路径/dsh-babel ``` 也可以在 DSH Desktop 里走 **设置 → 插件 → 添加插件**，填入仓库地址或本地路径。 安装后默认 **dry-run**：只在日志里打印兼容性报告，**不注册任何东西**。 ## 配置 配置项由 schemastery schema 声明，因此会出现在 **设置 → 插件 → dsh-babel** 的配置界面里： | 配置项 | 默认 | 说明 | |---|---|---| | `roots` | `[]` | 扫描根目录；字符串路径或 `{ source, path }`。留空时使用默认的 Claude / Codex 插件目录 | | `dryRun` | `true` | 只报告，不注册。要真正注册必须先设为 `false` | | `logReport` | `true` | 把兼容性报告打印到日志 | | `registerCommands` | `false` | 注册发现到的斜杠命令（需 `dryRun: false`） | | `registerMcp` | `false` | 注册预检通过（`severity: ok`）的 MCP 服务器（需 `dryRun: false`） | 开启真注册： ```yaml config: dryRun: false registerCommands: true registerMcp: true ``` ## 兼容矩阵（诚实版） | 外部形态 | 覆盖 | 说明 | |---|---|---| | MCP `.mcp.json`（stdio） | ✅ 高 | 免密钥、依赖命令存在的，基本可用 | | MCP `.mcp.json`（http/sse） | ✅ 高 | 依赖 bearer token 的会标「需密钥」 | | MCP（依赖宿主运行时变量） | ⚠️ 有损 | `CODEX_*` / `CLAUDE_*` 等对方宿主注入的变量，DSH 没有，标为不可用 | | MCP（OAuth） | ❌ 无对应 | `oauth_resource` 等 DSH 无等价物，丢弃并告知 | | 技能 `skills/*/SKILL.md` | ✅ 高 | 格式统一（由 skills-manager 等已有实现覆盖） | | 斜杠命令 `commands/*` | ✅ 已实现 | 发现 + 归一化 + 报告 + 注册 | | Hooks | ⚠️ 有损 | DSH 仅 7 个点、仅 command handler | | 子代理 `agents/*` | ⚠️ 降级 | DSH 无注册接口，只能降级为技能 | | 插件 UI / mods | ❌ 不支持 | 必须用 DSH client 插件重写，无法移植 | ## 报告长什么样 在一台装了 Claude Code 与 Codex 插件的机器上，首次加载会打印： ``` === dsh-babel 兼容性报告 === 文件: 28 服务器: 28 方言: {"bare":14,"wrapped":14} 传输: {"stdio":17,"streamable-http":11} 结论: 可用 14 / 需密钥 5 / 不可用 9 ✗ 不可用 (9): laravel-boost [stdio] BLOCKED - [command] command not on PATH: php terraform [stdio] BLOCKED - [daemon] docker installed but not running (no socket / probe failed) - [secret] missing credential: TFE_TOKEN codex_app [stdio] BLOCKED - [env] depends on CODEX_MCP_NODE_PATH (other-harness runtime), not available in DSH ``` 这就是这个插件的第二个价值：**明确告诉你为什么跑不起来**，而不是让用户以为「DSH 很烂」。 ## 目录结构 ``` index.js 插件入口（apply + schemastery Config，Cordis 宿主插件形式） cordis.patch.yml bundle patch（插入 dsh-babel 一行） locale/zh.json 卡片展示文案（标题 + 简介） locale/en.json same, in English icon.svg 插件图标 lib/normalize.mjs 内核：方言 → IR lib/discover.mjs 发现：遍历文件系统找声明 lib/preflight.mjs 预检：命令 / daemon / 密钥 / 版本 lib/secrets.mjs 密钥解析：env 为主 + 钥匙串白名单兜底 lib/commands.mjs 命令归一化：.md / .toml → 命令 IR lib/register.mjs 命令注册：ctx.commands.register + 参数替换 lib/register-mcp.mjs MCP 注册：连接 + createMcpToolDefinition + 工具注册 lib/report.mjs 报告：聚合 + 文本渲染 bin/dsh-babel.mjs CLI runner（本地测试用） test/ 单测 + 冒烟 docs/ 详细文档 CHANGELOG.md 版本变更记录 ``` ## 开发与测试 ```bash npm test # 全部单测（75 断言） node test/mcp-smoke.mjs # MCP 注册冒烟（需本地 symlink 到 DSH 包 + 真实服务器） node bin/dsh-babel.mjs # 直接跑一次报告 ``` ## 文档 - [功能详解](docs/FEATURES.md) - [配置参考](docs/CONFIG.md) - [兼容性说明](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md) - [架构与中间表示](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) - [版本变更](CHANGELOG.md) ## 许可证 [MIT](LICENSE)

plugins.description: Deep Feishu / Lark integration for DeepSeek Harness: Bitable (multidimensional tables), docs, sheets, wiki, drive, messages, plus a visual settings page.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-feishu

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Deep **Feishu / Lark** integration for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).

It gives the agent eight tools that act on a real Feishu tenant (and a browser
panel that shows what it did and fixes authorization in one click):

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `feishu_bitable` | Create **Bitable (多维表格)** apps with their tables and fields in one call; list tables and fields; insert, search, update, and delete records in batches |
| `feishu_dashboard` | Create dashboards and **chart blocks** inside a Bitable (柱状图 / 折线图 / 饼图 / 排行榜 / 指标卡 / NPS … 15 types), position them, and read a chart's computed numbers |
| `feishu_query` | Run a **grouped, aggregated query** over a table (group by, sum / avg / min / max / count / distinct_count, filter, sort, top-N) with the aggregation done server-side |
| `feishu_doc` | Create documents; append Markdown (converted to native blocks), append raw blocks, read plain text, or import a local Markdown/Word/Excel/PowerPoint/PDF file as a new cloud document |
| `feishu_sheet` | Create spreadsheets; add sheets; read, write, and append ranges |
| `feishu_drive` | Browse folders, create folders, upload and download files, move, delete, read metadata |
| `feishu_wiki` | List wiki spaces and nodes, resolve a wiki token to its document, create and move nodes |
| `feishu_message` | Send text, interactive cards, rich posts, files, and images; reply in a thread; post through a custom-bot webhook |
| `feishu_auth` | Diagnose authorization, produce the authorization URL, complete a manual code exchange, refresh, and log out |
| `feishu_api` | Call any documented Feishu open-platform path, with the same auth, retry, and error mapping |

New content lands in **the user's own cloud drive** because the tools act as the
authorized user, not as the app. When no user grant is stored they fall back to
the app identity and say so in a warning rather than silently filing documents
into a space the user cannot see.

---

## Quick start

### 1. Create a Feishu app

1. Open the [Feishu Open Platform](https://open.feishu.cn/app) (or
   [Lark](https://open.larksuite.com/app)) and create a **custom app**.
2. Under **凭证与基础信息**, note the **App ID** and **App Secret**.
3. Under **安全设置 → 重定向 URL**, add the callback this plugin serves:

   ```
   http://127.0.0.1:19387/api/feishu/oauth/callback
   ```

   The port is whatever DeepSeek Harness serves on (the plugin reads it from the
   host and reports the exact URI in `feishu_auth` action `status`).
4. Under **权限管理**, add the scopes below, then **publish a version** — scopes
   only apply after the version is released:

   | Scope | Needed for |
   |---|---|
   | `offline_access` | **Required** — without it Feishu returns no refresh token and the user must re-authorize every couple of hours |
   | `bitable:app` | Bitable |
   | `docx:document` | Documents |
   | `drive:drive` | Drive, imports, uploads |
   | `sheets:spreadsheet` | Spreadsheets |
   | `wiki:wiki` | Wiki |
   | `im:message`, `im:resource` | Messages and file/image sending |
   | `contact:user.base:readonly` | Reading the authorized user's name |

### 2. Enable the plugin

See [Install](#install) below, then restart DeepSeek Harness.

### 3. Configure it in the GUI

Open **设置 → 飞书 / Feishu**. Everything is editable there — no YAML by hand:

- **应用凭据** — the App ID, the App Secret (write-only), the credential
  reference name, and the brand (飞书 / Lark).
- **默认落点与身份** — the folder new content lands in, and which identity the
  tools use by default.
- **功能开关** — whether the tools register, whether the HTTP routes mount,
  whether the floating panel shows, and the tool-name prefix.
- **授权** — the scopes to request and the redirect URL to register.
- **高级** — endpoint overrides and the page-size caps.

**Saving writes only this plugin's entry** in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`,
which the harness hot-reloads, so most changes apply without a restart. The App
Secret is *never* written to that file: it goes straight into the credential
store under the reference name, and the page only ever shows whether it is set.

### 4. Authorize

Press **授权飞书** on the settings page, or ask the agent to run `feishu_auth`
with action `authorize_url`. The browser lands on the callback, the grant is
stored, and every later call acts as that user. The same form shows the redirect
URL to register on the Feishu app and lists the scopes to grant.

> Host without a reachable browser callback (a remote or headless session)? Open
> the URL anywhere, then pass the `code` query parameter to `feishu_auth` with
> action `complete`.

---

## Install

Two ways, and they are alternatives — **do not do both.** Each creates a loader
entry with id `feishu`, and the loader rejects a composition that defines one id
twice with `duplicate loader entry id`.

### As a bundle (recommended)

The package declares a `dsh.bundle` patch, so a bundle-aware CLI installs and
mounts it in one step:

```sh
dsh plugin add github:2048lr/dsh-feishu
```

That appends `dsh-feishu` to `dsh.profile.bundles` and profile boot merges
[cordis.patch.yml](cordis.patch.yml), which inserts the plugin row. Nothing else
needs editing.

The settings page is aware of this: when the profile mounts the bundle, it writes
an **id-targeted config override** rather than a second `insert`, so saving from
the GUI never breaks the composition.

### By hand (no CLI)

The plugin must be resolvable from the profile's `node_modules`, so it is copied
there:

```powershell
# from the repository root
pwsh -File scripts/install.ps1
```

The script copies the package into the profile's `node_modules` and inserts the
entry into `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: feishu
      name: dsh-feishu
      config:
        appId: cli_xxxxxxxxxxxx
        # appSecretRef: FEISHU_APP_SECRET
        # brand: feishu          # or lark
        # defaultFolderToken: fldcnxxxxxxxx
```

**Restart DeepSeek Harness.** The host half is a Node module cached in-process,
so a reload alone does not pick it up. The browser half reloads with the page.

After that first restart, use **设置 → 飞书 / Feishu** instead of editing the YAML:
the page rewrites the block the installer added and the harness hot-reloads it.

### Why the package avoids `@deepseek-ai/*` imports

A third-party plugin is loaded from a junction or a copied directory inside the
profile, where a bare `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` specifier resolves to whichever
DSH installation is reachable — which may not be the running host. The host half
therefore imports **only Node builtins** and hand-writes its tool definitions
and its configuration validation. The test suite checks every generated schema
against the real SDK validator, so the hand-written form cannot drift from what
the registry accepts.

---

## Configuration

All fields are optional except `appId`.

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `appId` | — | The Feishu app id. Required. |
| `appSecretRef` | `FEISHU_APP_SECRET` | Credential reference resolved through the harness credential store, then the environment. |
| `appSecret` | `''` | Literal fallback. Discouraged: it puts a secret in configuration. |
| `brand` | `feishu` | `feishu` (open.feishu.cn) or `lark` (open.larksuite.com). |
| `apiBaseUrl` / `accountsBaseUrl` | per brand | Override the endpoints (for a proxy or a private gateway). |
| `defaultFolderToken` | `''` | Where new documents, sheets, Bitable apps, and uploads go when a call omits a folder. |
| `defaultIdentity` | `auto` | `auto`, `user`, or `app`. `auto` uses the user when authorized and otherwise the app, reporting the fallback. |
| `toolPrefix` | `feishu_` | Rename the tools (for example `fs_`). |
| `requestTimeoutMs` | `30000` | Per-attempt timeout. |
| `maxRetries` | `2` | Total attempts for rate-limited or transient failures (capped at 6). |
| `enableTools` | `true` | Register the model-facing tools. |
| `enableOAuth` | `true` | Mount the `/api/feishu/*` routes (status, activity, config, OAuth). |
| `enableUi` | `true` | Show the floating panel. |
| `oauthRedirectUri` | auto | Override the callback. Empty means "use

# dsh-claude-code-theme **Claude Desktop's visual language for the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI.** Warm paper neutrals, terracotta accent, readable prose, quiet layered surfaces and a continuous composer — applied through DSH's own theme extension point, not by patching its stylesheets. [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-claude-code-theme.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-claude-code-theme) [![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/dsh-claude-code-theme.svg)](./LICENSE)
## Before and after Stock DSH — right-aligned bubble on a blue-tinted canvas, soft 12–28px corners, a floating composer with a circular send button: With the theme — a deeper sidebar, a raised right-hand panel, prose set for reading, compact tool summaries, and a continuous composer: Light mode, on Claude's cream canvas with white raised sheets: --- ## Install ```sh dsh plugin install dsh-claude-code-theme ``` Or add the row to your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` and its package to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`: ```yaml - insert: - id: claude-code-theme name: dsh-claude-code-theme ``` Reload the Web GUI. There is nothing to switch on: the theme composes over whichever palette you already use, so `light`, `dark` and `system` all keep working. ## What changes **Colour.** DSH's design system has three token tiers, and the theme works on all three: | Tier | What it is | What the theme does | | --- | --- | --- | | `--dsw-static-*` | The raw colour ramps | Retints DSH's blue-tinted greys to Claude's warm paper greys, and DeepSeek blue to terracotta. The alias tier resolves through these, so this alone recolours most of the application. | | `--dsw-alias-*` | The semantic roles components consume | Pins the roles Claude treats differently: a cream canvas under raised sheets, a terracotta primary button and focus ring, warm hairlines, and text that stops short of pure white on dark. | | `--dsw-specific-*` | Named surfaces | Retunes the sidebar, composer, bubbles, menus and code surfaces. | **Surface hierarchy.** Claude Desktop stacks depth rather than flattening it, so the theme gives each column its own level instead of one shared grey: | Region | Dark | Light | | --- | --- | --- | | Sidebar | `#111110` (deepest) | `#f5f3ec` | | Canvas | `#171716` | `#faf9f5` | | Raised sheets — cards, composer, right panel | `#1d1d1b` | `#ffffff` | The right panel becomes a raised sheet separated by a hairline instead of floating as a detached card. **Geometry.** DSH routes **280 `border-radius` declarations through six `--dsw-radius-*` tokens** (measured across all 179 shipped UI bundles), so the theme re-points the scale itself: | Token | DSH | Theme | | --- | --- | --- | | `--dsw-radius-xs` | 4px | 4px | | `--dsw-radius-sm` | 8px | 6px | | `--dsw-radius-md` | 12px | 8px | | `--dsw-radius-lg` | 16px | 12px | | `--dsw-radius-xl` | 20px | 16px | | `--dsw-radius-panel` | 28px | 20px | The corners that bypass the scale are reached through the stable `data-slot` and `data-*` hooks rather than a build hash. **Typography.** This is the part that most decides whether the result reads as a product or as a costume. Claude Desktop is a reading surface, so the transcript is set in the UI sans at a comfortable line height, and monospace is kept for the things that are actually code: | | Treatment | | --- | --- | | Assistant prose | UI sans, 1.65 line height, normal heading letter-spacing | | Inline code, code blocks, tool output | Monospace | | Sidebar, header, composer | UI sans | | Code-block banner | Sentence case, not shouted uppercase | **Transcript.** Your turn is a right-aligned bubble on a quiet surface; the assistant's is prose on the canvas; tool calls collapse into single-line summaries (`Ran 2 commands ›`) that expand in place, which is how Claude Desktop keeps a long working session scannable. **Composer.** One continuous rounded surface: the editor and the controls share a single card with no divider between them, the submit control is a circle, and focus draws a soft terracotta ring rather than a hard outline. **Chrome.** Quiet navigation rows instead of an elevated primary button, hover states limited to enabled controls, `focus-visible` rings for keyboard use, and thin warm scrollbars. ## Customisation Everything the component layer decides reads a `--cct-*` property declared once on `body`, so you can retune it from your own CSS without patching the package: ```css body { /* A serif reading face, the way long-form prose is often set. */ --cct-prose: Georgia, "Songti SC", serif; /* Roomier or tighter surfaces. */ --cct-composer-radius: 24px; --cct-control-radius: 6px; --cct-editor-inset: 20px; } ``` | Knob | Default | Purpose | | --- | --- | --- | | `--cct-sans` | system UI stack | UI face, including the sidebar and composer | | `--cct-prose` | `var(--cct-sans)` | Face used for assistant prose only | | `--cct-mono` | DSH's code stack | Code, tool output and paths | | `--cct-control-radius` | `8px` | Buttons, rows, chips, code blocks | | `--cct-composer-radius` | `18px` | The composer surface | | `--cct-editor-inset` | `16px` | Composer text inset from its edge | | `--cct-focus` | brand primary | Focus ring colour | To retune colours instead, stack your own layer on top — later layers win per token: ```js ctx.theme.overrideTokens('my-tweaks', { '--dsw-alias-brand-primary': { light: '#c96442', dark: '#d97757' }, }) ``` ## How it works The plugin is a browser half plus an inert host row. The browser half (`lib/client.js`) does exactly two things, both inside one Cordis effect, so unloading or HMR removes the theme completely: 1. Calls `ctx.theme.overrideTokens('dsh-claude-code-theme', …)` with 174 tokens as `{ light, dark }` pairs. This is DSH's documented third-party theme extension point. The service stacks the layer over the active palette and `ui-layout` writes it as inline custom properties on `` — which is why the theme outranks the base palette sheets without `!important`, and why overriding the `--dsw-static-*` ramps propagates to every alias that resolves through them. 2. plugins.description: Open-source, local-first envelope messaging for DeepSeek Harness: a TypeScript node, human-first inbox, explainable collaborator discovery, and bounded LAN recovery.
plugins.readme_text:
# Linko

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Linko is open-source, local-first envelope messaging for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). It helps agents find the right collaborator, exchange scoped context, and continue a task under explicit human-controlled policies.

Linko is an early runnable MVP. The repository remains specification-driven: product boundaries, state transitions, delivery recovery, privacy rules, and architecture decisions are written beside the runtime.

## Why Linko

LAN messaging and approval panels are useful building blocks. Linko adds the part that becomes more useful with a person's own evidence and context:

- Each person and Agent can keep a subjective set of capability claims; later releases may attach signatures without creating a global reputation score.
- A task query can produce a local recommendation with evidence and an explanation.
- Context is shared by scope and purpose instead of being broadcast as a complete private history.
- A person can answer an inbound request, ask their Agent to draft a reply, or delegate a bounded response policy.
- Every delivery is a small envelope with a human-readable cover, machine-readable semantics, and an optional local body or safe surface.
- The experimental first group profile is capped at 500 member principals, with group delivery and message-layer E2EE as separate milestones.

## Project status

The MVP runs a SQLite-backed node and a human-first envelope inbox. It supports an explicit two-node HTTPS pairing profile with a durable outbox, pinned certificates, bearer authentication, retry-safe command IDs, and REST recovery. The local node also exposes an advisory loopback WebSocket for live UI hints; paired WSS delivery remains a later milestone. The replaceable TypeScript DSH companion bridge now provides `ask`, `inbox`, `inspect`, `draft`, `approve`, and `reply` adapters over the local API. Message signatures and E2EE remain later milestones; this is not a 20,000-node capacity claim.

- Product scope: [English](docs/specs/0001-product-scope.md) · [中文](docs/specs/0001-product-scope.zh.md)
- Architecture: [English](docs/architecture.md) · [中文](docs/architecture.zh.md)
- State and storage: [English](docs/specs/0005-state-and-storage.md) · [中文](docs/specs/0005-state-and-storage.zh.md)
- Review record: [English](docs/review.md) · [中文](docs/review.zh.md)
- Roadmap: [English](ROADMAP.md) · [中文](ROADMAP.zh.md)
- Decisions: [English](docs/decisions/README.md) · [中文](docs/decisions/README.zh.md)
- Local node MVP: [English](packages/node/README.md) · [中文](packages/node/README.zh.md)
- DSH companion bridge: [English](packages/bridge/README.md) · [中文](packages/bridge/README.zh.md)
- Envelope inbox UI: [English](packages/web/DESIGN.md) · [中文](packages/web/DESIGN.zh.md)

## Design direction

The first physical store is one SQLite database behind one TypeScript node. Immutable event content is durable; delivery attempts, read state, approvals, and notifications are local operational state. REST cursor synchronization and the SQLite outbox remain the canonical recovery path. The approved [2026 transport decision](docs/decisions/0010-wss-live-session-and-recovery.md) selects WSS as the online live session; its implementation remains pending. A graph can be materialized later as a view over claims; a graph database is not required.

The network uses ordinary IP and authenticated TCP/TLS connections, with explicit pairing. mDNS/DNS-SD is an optional discovery hint only; it does not grant trust or carry message bodies. Linko adds no application-layer router or payload flooding, and requires no Linko-specific router or switch feature. WebTransport/QUIC remain deferred experiments alongside DHT, Merkle synchronization, full-mesh sockets, blockchain consensus, and Rust/WASM; each needs a measured reason and a fallback test.

## DeepSeek Harness fit

Linko is intended to be a community plugin and companion protocol for the DeepSeek Harness ecosystem. It follows the Harness model that capabilities are composable plugins, while keeping the Linko protocol independently usable by other agents and clients.

## Contributing

Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and the repository guidance in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Early contributions are most useful as design review, threat modeling, interoperability experiments, and small protocol fixtures.

## Topics

The repository is indexed with dsh, dsh-plugin, deepseek-harness, agent-collaboration, local-first, lan-messaging, envelope-messaging, human-in-the-loop, sqlite, typescript, and pnpm.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

plugins.description: Output house rules for every DeepSeek Harness agent: no check-mark or cross glyphs in replies or written files, and a light kaomoji habit in conversation. One global prompt section, so every preset, workspace and subagent obeys without a single preset edit.
plugins.readme_text:
# Oishikunaare-Moe-Moe-Kyun

> Chinese documentation: [README.zh-CN.md](README.zh-CN.md)

Output house rules for an AI agent: one core, and four ways to reach it. The rules are about how an
agent writes - judgement glyphs, emoji, the kaomoji habit, the language it thinks in - and none of that
is specific to one harness, so the package is not either.

| entry | what it is | how it is wired |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **CLI** `mmk` | `rules`, `lib`, `check`, `notice`, `voice`, `review`, `wire` | a shell, a git hook, CI, or a person asking whether a line would be refused. Exit 3 means a breach |
| **MCP server** | `mmk_rules`, `mmk_check`, `mmk_notice` and the `mmk://rules` resource | any MCP client, no assumption about which agent is on the other side |
| **Claude Code hook** | corrects a breach while the turn is still open | `Stop` answers `{"decision":"block","reason":<notice>}`, `UserPromptSubmit` and `SessionStart` attach context |
| **DSH plugin** | one global system prompt section for a whole profile | mounted once by the roster, so it reaches every preset, workspace, conversation and subagent |
| **modules** | `oishikunaare-moe-moe-kyun/portable`, `/transcripts` | writing another adapter: all of the above are thin layers over those two files |

`mmk wire <target>` prints the wiring for a specific place - the hook block, the MCP client block, the
`AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` / `GEMINI.md` rules block, the DSH plugin row - with real paths filled in.

### What is verified where

An entry that has never met the thing it is written for is not the same as one that has, and the
difference is worth stating instead of implying. This table is the honest version.

| entry | how it is verified |
| --- | --- |
| DSH plugin | In production on the machine this was written on: mounted in a live profile, and its rules and self-check are visible in real sessions |
| CLI `mmk` | Used on that machine for real work - auditing a session, answering whether a line would be refused - and exercised by `test/portable.mjs` |
| MCP server | The protocol is checked locally: a handshake, `tools/list`, every tool called, `resources/read`. The client half depends on the client |
| Claude Code hook | **Documented contract plus recorded fixtures only** (`npm run test:adapters`); never run against a live Claude Code, because none is installed here. The contract has moved between releases, so treat this one as a candidate rather than a supported entry |
| rules files (`mmk wire ...-md`) | The block is generated from the same resolved rules the plugin serves, so the text is verified; whether a given program reads that file is its own documentation |

When a harness that is not on this machine does become available, the way to close the gap is one
recorded payload: save the stdin JSON a hook actually receives as `adapters/fixtures/<harness>/<case>.json`
and `npm run test:adapters` replays it. That is what the fixture directory is for, and it is why adding
an adapter is cheap once someone can run the client - and why writing five of them from memory would not
be.

The DSH plugin row is worth explaining, because it is the anti-drift argument: a profile-level plugin is
mounted once by the roster, so the section it registers reaches every agent that joins that standing
scope - every preset, every workspace, every new conversation, and subagents too. That is why it is done
there rather than in fifteen preset files: a preset is a copy, and a copy is a thing that drifts. The
other entries exist because the same rules are worth having where no such roster exists.

Four rules ship today.

1. **Symbol discipline** - no check-mark or cross judgement glyphs, in a reply or in a file the agent
   writes. Those glyphs pollute context and regression parameters, and a file written today is read
   back into context tomorrow, so the ban covers files and not just replies. Say it in words instead:
   pass / fail, works / broken, applied / not applied, yes / no.
2. **No emoji** - zero, in replies, in the agent's own thinking and in every file it writes. The ban
   is by block rather than by character list (pictographs, faces, transport, Miscellaneous Symbols,
   the geometric shapes that carry emoji presentation, plus the variation selector, the zero width
   joiner and the skin tone modifiers), because a list would need regenerating every Unicode release
   and would still be incomplete. Decoration is carved out - a heart, a note, a star, a sparkle, a
   flower - so the ban admits exactly the code points the loaded palette uses.
3. **Kaomoji habit** - Japanese-style emoticons in conversation and in the agent's own thinking, at a
   floor rather than as garnish: at least one per three sentences, and any reply of two sentences or
   more carries one. Aim above the floor. Faces rotate rather than repeat, and places that take none
   take none - a stack trace, a table of numbers, a serious conclusion.
4. **Thinking language** - think and answer in the user's own language instead of defaulting to
   English, which is not a neutral metalanguage: a Chinese conversation reasoned about in English is
   exactly the habit the rule exists to replace. Chinese gets Chinese with Japanese particles and
   terminology mixed in where they fall naturally; Japanese gets Japanese. English is available in one
   case only, the moe-fandom register - romanized Japanese words (kawaii, sugoi, moe, senpai, yabai,
   baka), fandom English (nya~, ehehe, ufufu, desu wa, the honorifics -chan / -san / -sama), waves and
   long vowels, alongside the kaomoji palette. Dry technical English is not that register. The reason
   is in the rule: the grammar and the logic of English do not match the habits of moe-fandom culture.
   It covers thinking and replies, and it never buys a fandom register with correctness - technical
   content stays accurate. File contents, code, commands and commit messages still carry no tone.

Rule 4 differs from 1-3 in one mechanical way: it is not a per-rule override. `bannedSymbols`,
`kaomoji` and the `rules` object replace the rules they name, while the thinking-language block is
appended after them (and before `append`), because "mount this plugin and the agent thinks in the
user's language" is the promise of mounting it. `enabled: false` is what takes it away.

## Where this package takes its material from

This is a standard for **MMK itself** - the source of the markers, the palette and the prose it
ships - not a rule the plugin hands to an agent. Nothing here is injected into a prompt.

- **Taken**: moe-fandom culture of 1990-2015 - 90s bishoujo games and OVAs, 2000s galge and light
  novels, VOCALOID and doujin music, 2000s-2010s anime, and the mid-2010s "yami-kawaii" look. The
  traditional moe attributes stay available: tsundere, natural airhead, frail, denpa, chuunibyou,
  keigo and the rest.
- **Not taken**: the "jirai-kei" (landmine type) aesthetic that formed from 2018 onward and what grew
  out of it - jirai make-up, the ryousangata look, the menhera-flavoured dependent and possessive
  romance aesthetic. The criterion is *pragmatics and aesthetics that formed and spread after 2018*,
  not the presence of one particular word: a term is not disqualified for being old, and a style is
  not admitted for being spelled with old characters.
- **Excluded outright: fandom for boys-love** (BL / danmei / yaoi) and its own vocabulary. This one is
  unconditional, with no middle ground to argue about.
- **Also excluded outright**: grotesque and guro material, and the fetish registers that grew beside
  it - ryou-naissance injury content, scatological content, body modification and dismemberment of that
  kind, and SM.
- **The exemption that sits under those exclusions**: being explicit is not what is excluded.
  **Ordinary R18 adult material is not something this package avoids**, and a reader should not quietly
  widen an exclusion above to cover it.
- **A soft preference, not a fourth exclusion: hygiene awareness.** Where the register can be chosen at
  all, steer around - preferentially decline rather than forbid - the R18 practices that carry a
  hygiene or safety implication (anal, oral-to-deep-t

plugins.description: Normify · DSH 插件：把项目架构写成归一化的分形模块树，三层校验（写时 / 校验 / 冻结回执）、30 个 normify_* 工具 + normify-gen 技能，一键渲染单文件交互式架构图；支持伴随式开发（change_open → brief → check → 实施 → refresh → change_close）。
plugins.readme_text:
English · 简体中文

Normify · 归一化框架图构建器

把整个项目描述成一棵"人机共读"的分形模块树：AI 负责分析与创作，确定性引擎负责校验、编译与渲染 —— 点开任意模块，就是一张更精细的子图。

--- ## 0. 一句话 Normify 是 **DeepSeek Harness（DSH）插件**，也是**一套写给 AI 用的开发流程**： - **给 AI 的**：`normify-gen` 技能 + **31 个 `normify_*` 工具** —— 让模型把仓库分析成模块树结构数据， 并在后续开发中**先建图后编程、伴随编程改图**（计划态建树 → 逐个实现 → 关单收尾）。 - **给引擎的**：零容忍校验（L1 写时 / L2 全项目 / L3 冻结）+ 确定性编译（`tree.json` 等四件产物，SHA-256 冻结） + 渲染数据（`renders/`，决定"每一层怎么画"）。 - **给人的**：**单文件交互式架构图**（`normify.html`）—— 逐层下钻、悬停看介绍、一键中英切换、深链接、 多树、**API 直连箭头**、跨层聚合、缩放与搜索。零依赖，双击即开。 > 它不是"生成一张图就结束"的工具：结构数据与代码**互为契约**，每次改动都能被 `normify_sync` 检出漂移， > 并以 `normify_change_close`（**0 error 强制**）收尾，让"代码 → 架构图"永远同步。


引擎层：14 个模块、API 直连箭头（箭头锚定到具体 API 行）、带标签的子系统依赖、跨层聚合虚线

## 1. 它解决什么问题 | 痛点 | Normify 的做法 | | --- | --- | | 架构图一画完就过期 | 结构数据是**可校验的源数据**：`normify_sync` 按 `fingerprint` 检出漂移，`normify_change_close` 强制 0 error 收尾 | | 图太粗，看不出接口契约 | 粒度到**单一功能单元**，API 写在叶子上，箭头可锚定到具体 API（`from_api`/`to_api`） | | AI 改代码时"看不见全局" | `normify_brief` 给出目标模块契约、影响面（谁依赖我）、规则约束与验收清单 | | 设计先写代码后补文档，必然漂移 | **计划态先建树**（`state: planned`）→ 实现后 `normify_module_refresh(activate)` 自动转 active | | 结构规范靠人自觉 | `policy.yml` 架构规则（依赖方向 / 禁依赖 / 无环 / 深度 / 跨树 / 命名）由 `validate` 强制执行 | | 大仓库一次生成太重 | 增量再生成：只重建受影响子树，`layouts_to_review` 点名要复核的层 | ## 2. 核心特性 ### 2.1 数据模型：分形 + 零冗余 - **唯一元素**：整个数据库由无数个结构完全相同的**基本模块**构成（每个模块 = 一个 Markdown 文件）。 - **只存 `parent`**：单方向引用，`children` 由索引导出 —— 不会出现"父子各说各话"。 - **API 只在叶子存一次**：聚合、统计、索引全部是编译期派生数据（`tree.json` / `api-index.json`）。 - **两类边**：containment（树边，导航骨架）+ dependency（箭头，可跨子树、跨树，按 `kind` 着色）。 - **路径式 id + 不变 uid**：AI 沿 id 逐层定位（类二分查找）；`uid` 在改名/移动时保持不变，git diff 稳定。 - **深度不设上限**（0.5.0 起）：想有多细就拆多细，深度不再成为"合并模块"的理由。 ### 2.2 三层校验，fail-closed | 层 | 时机 | 内容 | | --- | --- | --- | | **L1** | 每次写入 | 必填字段、id 文法、uid、parent 一致性、双语长度、source/apis/deps 形状、state/replacement | | **L2** | `normify_validate` | 全项目：唯一性、文件↔id 映射、叶子/非叶子规则、API 键唯一、依赖目标、环、渲染数据交叉校验、架构规则、变更日志、（可选）仓库证据（source 存在性 + 指纹一致） | | **L3** | `normify_build` | 任何 error 都不产出产物；产出即 SHA-256 冻结进 `receipt.json` | 每条诊断都带 `severity / code / message / subject / evidence / supportedFixes` —— **AI 可自行修复**。 ### 2.3 渲染器：单文件、可下钻、API 直连 - 单文件 HTML（内联 CSS/JS，**零外部依赖**、零遥测），双击即开，可直接归档/发人。 - 逐层下钻 + 面包屑 + 搜索（模块名/API）+ 大纲视图 + API 浏览器。 - **API 直连**：叶子框内展示 API 明细行，箭头锚定到具体 API 行的端口；同一 API 行上的多条边自动扇形分离。 - 跨层依赖聚合为虚线 `×N`（默认隐藏，工具栏或 `?agg=1` 开启，悬停看明细）。 - 深链接：`#module=`、`#api=`、`#view=outline`、`?lang=zh|en`、`?agg=1`；缩放 / 悬停高亮 / 明暗主题。 - **几何自检**：仓库自带 `check-geometry.mjs`，逐层断言"线不出界 / 不贴框 / 不穿框 / 不压线"。 ### 2.4 伴随开发：先建图后编程 ``` change_open → brief → check → module_batch(state=planned) → 【写代码】 → module_refresh(activate) → change_close(0 error 强制) → verified + revision.after ``` - **计划态**：源码还不存在也能先建树（`fingerprint: pending`），`validate` 放行； - **禁止假激活**：源码没落地就 `activate` 直接被拒； - **收尾即闭环**：`change_close` 会刷新指纹 → 校验（0 error 强制）→ 编译（可选渲染）→ 标记 `verified`， 任何一步失败都不关闭，变更保持原状态； - **改图随代码**：`normify_sync` 用 `git diff` + 未跟踪文件定位受影响模块与指纹漂移，`module_patch` 跟随更新。 ### 2.5 架构规则先行（policy.yml） | 规则 | 作用 | | --- | --- | | `dependency-direction` | 层顺序即允许的依赖方向（如 plugin → tools → engine），可控制同层是否允许 | | `forbid-dependency` | 禁止某些 from → to 的依赖（可按 kind / state 过滤） | | `acyclic` | 依赖图禁止成环（可含跨树） | | `max-depth` | id 段数上限（**可选**：不写就是不限，0.5.0 起默认不限） | | `cross-tree` | 跨树依赖策略：`forbid` / `allow` / `require-to-api` | | `naming` | 作用域内 id 段的命名正则 | 安装后 `normify_validate` / `normify_build` / `normify_check` 全部强制执行；**违规先改设计，不能绕过**。 ## 3. 最新变化 ### v0.5.4 · 把"第二轮 A/B 实测"暴露的 4 个工具缺陷修掉（当前版本） 第二轮 A/B 换了题目（**表格公式引擎 + CLI**，同一份规范、隐藏黑盒 88 项、外加**差分模糊测试**）。 两组最终 B 88/88、A 87/88（差异只有一条 §5.2 语义）；这一版修的是**工具侧**新暴露的 4 个坑： - **`mode:"patch"` 的静默 no-op 被拦下**：原来 `items:[{patch:{id, tags:[...]}}]`（少一层包装）会返回 `ok:true, count:1` 却**一个字段都没改**——最危险的"假成功"。现在直接报 `args/invalid-patch`， evidence 里给出收到的键与正确形状 `{patch:{id, patch:{...}}}`；单模块 `normify_module_patch` 传空补丁 同样报 `args/empty-patch`（只给 `expect_updated_at` 也不再静默通过）。 - **`normify_module_refresh` 不再强依赖 git**：`repoRoot` 不是 git 仓库时，以前直接 `refresh/git-failed` 失败（实测中 AI 只能 `git init` 才能激活模块）。现在改成**降级**：指纹照常重算、 `state` 照常激活，`revision` 保持模块原值，并给出 `refresh/git-unavailable` 警告与修法。 - **`change_open` 的 `acceptance` 报错具体化**：以前把 `{zh,en}` 写进 acceptance 只有一句笼统报错； 现在明确写出"**第 N 条不是非空字符串（收到 …）：验收标准只接受纯字符串**"，并提示双语描述写进 `title`/`intent`。 - **`normify_help` 支持 `topic:"tool:<工具名>"`**：`tools` 主题现在每个工具都带**必填/可选**摘要， 新主题可按需打印**完整参数树**（类型 / 描述 / 必填，由注册表实时生成、与运行时校验同源）。 实测里 AI 为确认 `mode=patch` 的嵌套形状去读了插件源码——这条主题正是为了消灭这种绕路。 ### v0.5.3 · 把「伴随编程实测」暴露的 4 个摩擦点修掉 这四个问题来自一次真实的 A/B 对照实验：两个 AI 用同一份规范写同一个后端，一个带插件走伴随流程、一个纯手写 （最终代码在隐藏黑盒验收上都是 **42/42**）。插件组多交付了 41 模块 / 110 API / 10 层的结构数据，但也踩到了下面 4 个坑： - **`normify_help` 支持 `topic`**：此前它完全忽略入参，只返回同一份字段速查 —— 实测里 AI 为了拿准 `change_open` / `layout_upsert` / `change_close` 的参数名，只能去读插件源码（多花约 4 分钟）。 现在按主题返回：`fields`（默认）/ `deps`（箭头与 API 直连）/ `renders` / `flow`（伴随流程）/ `tools`（工具清单）/ `policy` / `errors`（常见诊断码与修法）/ `all`；**传错主题会直接报错并列出可用主题**，不再静默忽略。 - **项目初始化通道**：新增第 31 个工具 `normify_project_init` —— 建 `normify-/` + 默认架构规则， 可选 `root` 一步创建"计划态根模块"（幂等）；同时 `normify_change_open` 现在也会**自动建项目目录** （此前报 `project/no-modules`，AI 只能用 `module_batch {items:[],dry_run:true}` 绕过去）； `normify_brief` 遇到不存在的模块会给出"先 init / 先建树 / 改用 task"的可执行提示。 - **批量诊断的因果链**：一条 `label-too-long` 曾连带出 3 条 `dep/target-missing`（因为 L1 失败的模块会被移出批次工作集）， AI 只能去读源码才能确认根因。现在连带错误改报 `dep/target-dropped` / `structure/parent-dropped`， 在 message 与 evidence 里点明**根因诊断码**，并在失败响应的 `root_causes` 里直接列出被丢弃的模块（附 `hint`）。 - **「API 直连」引导**：两端都声明了 API 却没写 `from_api` / `to_api` 的箭头，`normify_validate` 会给出**聚合** warning `dep/unanchored`（条数 + 前 3 条示例）。这正是实验里被浪费的能力：110 条 API 声明，54 条箭头 0 条锚定 —— 不锚定，箭头就只能落在框边，钉不到 API 行上。**引导≠放宽**：锚错键仍然是 error。 ### v0.5.2 · 修掉三处会写坏数据的真实缺陷 - **`normify_module_upsert` 的必填表不再丢失**：`parameters.required` 恢复为 `["frontmatter"]`， `frontmatter` 的 9 个必填字段（uid / id / parent / name / description / source / revision / updated_at / fingerprint） 也重新出现在 schema 里。此前嵌套 schema 被二次编译，必填表被整段丢掉 —— 模型看到的约束与运行时实际校验不一致。 - **`normify_module_move` 迁移渲染数据时重写内容**：`id` / `order` / `groups.children` / `edge_hints` 全部改写到新 id， 并同步维护**旧父级**（删掉已迁出子模块的引用）与**新父级**（把新 id 补进 `order`）。 修复前：move 完之后项目立刻被 L2 判为 `layout/id-mismatch` + `layout/order-child` 等（实测 8–9 个 error，0.5.2 后为 0）。 - **晋升为容器时不再把 API 留在容器上**：叶子被晋升（显式 `normify_module_promote`、写子模块自动晋升、move 到叶子底下） 时，容器上残留的 `apis` 会被摘除，并回报 `structure/api-dropped-on-promote` 警告（附丢失的 API 键清单）—— 修复前项目会直接卡在 `api/non-leaf`。 - **API 默认全展开**：渲染数据字段 `max_api_rows` 缺省 **0 = 全部展开**，叶子上的 API 一行不折叠；需要收窄时显式写 1..48。 - 三处缺陷各自配了回归断言：`tests/regression-0.5.2.mjs`（34 项，全绿）。 ### v0.5.1 · 渲染器防重叠（线压线 12 → 0） - **修复连线共线重叠**：28 层合计 **12 处 → 0 处**。四处根因： ① 首选路由只判"不穿别人的框"，从不检查是否压到已画的线 → 改为只接受 `violations === 0` 的候选； ② API 锚定端口没有端口分离（同一 API 行被多条边共用） → 行内 ±5.5px 扇形分离； ③ API 端口落在上下边时被放进框内部 → 上下边退回按边均匀分离； ④ `segClear` 整块跳过源/目标框 → 新增"进入自身框内部"检查（内缩 2px）。 - 节点/分组间距 170 → 220，给密集层更多自由通道。 ### v0.5.0 · 取消模块数量上限 - **删除 `MAX_DEPTH = 12`** 硬限制：树可以一直下钻到"单一功能单元"；需要限层时用 `policy.yml` 的 `max-depth` 规则显式声明（`maxDepth` 放宽到 1..64）。 - SKILL：目标深度改为"不设上限"，单批上限 40 → 200，新增"每叶 API 尽量 3–5 条"的粒度指引。
更早的版本（v0.4.x / v0.3 / v0.2 / v0.1） - **v0.4.1**：渲染器 v3 定稿（自由通道走线、viewBox 全几何自适应、API 直连、跨层聚合、缩放与悬停）； `normify_sync` 识别**未跟踪的新文件**（`git ls-files --others`）。 - **v0.4.0**：伴随开发（`state: pla

plugins.description: TypeSafe Jev for DeepSeek Harness, the Model Context Protocol, and plain Node: typed judgments instead of prose, offline by default.
plugins.readme_text:
# jevcore
[![dshfind](https://dshfind.com/api/badge/PerryLink/jevcore?metric=downloads)](https://dshfind.com/plugins/PerryLink/jevcore?ref=badge)

[![DSH Market](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/2BingLing/dsh-market/master/assets/readme/badge-listed-en.svg)](https://dsh.market/)
[![OpenSSF Scorecard](https://api.securityscorecards.dev/projects/github.com/PerryLink/jevcore/badge)](https://api.securityscorecards.dev/projects/github.com/PerryLink/jevcore)
[![jevcore MCP server](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/PerryLink/jevcore/badges/score.svg)](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/PerryLink/jevcore)

TypeSafe [Jev](https://typesafe.ai) for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)
and any other MCP host.

Jev is not a chat model. It answers typed questions — `noul` (yes/no), `choice`, `score` — and returns
calibrated probabilities. It does not write prose, and asking it to is a category error. This project
gives an agent exactly that surface, and nothing more.

**Offline by default. Egress disclosed. Nothing default-on.**

---

**📖 Ecosystem knowledge base** — measured data, not marketing: [plugin development guide · plugin-selection data · maintenance criteria](https://perrylink.github.io/dsh-plugin-guide/).

<!-- star-cta -->
## ⭐ 如果它帮到了你

这个插件是 [DSH 插件家族](https://github.com/PerryLink)的一员（40+ 个，全部 Apache-2.0）。如果你在用，**给个 star** —— 它不会解锁任何功能，但会让下一个人在搜索里更容易找到它。

*English:* part of a 40+ plugin family for DeepSeek Harness. If it is useful, **a star helps the next person find it** — nothing is gated behind it.


## Three packages, one decision layer

| Package | What it is | Use it when |
|---|---|---|
| [`jevcore`](packages/core) | The decisions. Imports nothing from DeepSeek Harness or Cordis. | You want Jev in a plain script, a service, or your own harness |
| [`jevcore-dsh`](packages/dsh) | The DSH plugin: one service, three tools, two opt-in gates | You are running DeepSeek Harness |
| [`jevcore-mcp`](packages/mcp) | The same three tools over MCP, with a stdio binary | Your host speaks MCP but is not DSH |

The adapters are thin on purpose. `packages/dsh` is four files: it declares tool schemas and
translates hook payloads. Everything decision-shaped — the primitives, the providers, the egress
contract, the policy, the gates — lives in core, so a new adapter cannot drift from the guarantees
the others make.
One runtime requirement differs across the three: `jevcore-dsh` tracks the harness and needs
Node `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`, while `jevcore` and `jevcore-mcp` need `>=20`.

---

## Why this exists

Between 2026-09-17 and 09-20, nineteen plugins appeared that wire Jev into DSH. Auditing their source
found a consistent pattern: the module labelled *guard*, *gate*, or *warden* was also the module
shipping prompts, tool arguments, and file contents to a third party, and the README generally did not
say so. Several were enabled by default. One gate could be reconfigured by the model it was guarding.

This project is the same idea with those failure modes designed out:

| Property | How it is guaranteed here |
|---|---|
| No network call unless you ask for one | Default provider is an offline mock; the live path needs both `provider: live` and a resolved credential |
| Every transmission named before it happens | One startup log line per feature: `off` or `SENDS <feature> { fields }` |
| Gates register nothing when disabled | Verified by test, not by policy — a disabled gate adds no event listener at all |
| The model cannot widen its own constraints | No tool exposes gate configuration |
| A judge that cannot answer never means "allow" | Undecided resolves through explicit config, defaulting to `ask` |

---

## The egress contract

This is the part worth reading before installing.

Transmission is decided per feature, and every feature defaults to off. The plugin prints its own
contract at load:

```
[jevcore] provider=mock  endpoint=none  egress=OFF  (no network calls will be made; every answer is synthetic)
[jevcore] ready - provider=mock - gates: safety=off context=off
```

With `provider: live` and every feature enabled, the same report becomes explicit about what leaves:

```
[jevcore] provider=live  endpoint=https://api.typesafe.ai  egress=ON
[jevcore]   SENDS  tool:jev_ask  { state<=16000c questions<=4000c }
[jevcore]   SENDS  tool:jev_rank  { state<=16000c questions<=4000c }
[jevcore]   SENDS  tool:jev_check  { state<=16000c questions<=4000c }
[jevcore]   SENDS  gate:safety  { state<=8000c questions<=2000c }
[jevcore]   SENDS  gate:context  { state<=6000c questions<=2000c }
[jevcore]   redaction is best-effort; it removes named fields and known secret shapes, and cannot
             recognise an unrecognised secret in free text
```

| Feature | Off by default? | What it sends |
|---|---|---|
| `tool:jev_ask` | runs when the model calls it | the arguments the model passed, after redaction |
| `tool:jev_rank` | runs when the model calls it | the query plus every candidate |
| `tool:jev_check` | runs when the model calls it | the claim and its evidence |
| `gate:safety` | **yes — explicit opt-in** | the tool name, its arguments, the workspace root |
| `gate:context` | **yes — explicit opt-in** | a large tool result the agent just received |

The tools transmit only when the model chooses to call them, which is visible in the transcript. The
gates would run on every matching tool call, which is not, so they are opt-in.

### Redaction, and its honest limit

Before anything is sent, `src/redact.ts` runs two passes: values under sensitive field names
(`password`, `token`, `apiKey`, `authorization`, …) are replaced wholesale, and secret-shaped strings
that survive into free text are pattern-matched (`Bearer …`, `sk-…`, `ts_live_…`, AWS/GitHub/Google
key shapes, JWTs, private-key headers, credentials in connection strings).

This is a mitigation, not a permission. A secret that sits under an unrecognised key name *and* does
not match a known shape will pass through. If that possibility is unacceptable for your workload, do
not enable the live provider.

---

## Install

### As a DeepSeek Harness plugin

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add jevcore-dsh
```

Or from a checkout:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add /absolute/path/to/jevcore/packages/dsh
```

`packages/dsh` imports `jevcore` by name, so a checkout also needs core
resolvable from the profile (`add /absolute/path/to/jevcore/packages/core`).

Then confirm the row activated — the plugin list should show `jev` as `active`,
not `failed` — and check the startup report in the log.

### As an MCP server

For a host that speaks MCP, the same three tools are available over stdio:

```sh
npx -y jevcore-mcp
```

To wire it into DeepSeek Harness specifically, install a configuration-only bundle
whose patch inserts the harness's own MCP client:

```yml
- insert:
    - id: jev-mcp
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client'
      config:
        serverName: jev
        transport: stdio
        command: npx
        args: ['-y', 'jevcore-mcp']
        env:
          TYPESAFE_API_KEY: '<the key>'
        failOnStartupError: true
```

The env map is not optional: DSH strips every credential-shaped name — anything
containing KEY, PASSWORD, SECRET or TOKEN, in any case — from the environment it
hands a spawned server, then merges this map back in afterwards. A key exported in
your shell never arrives, and the server stays on the offline mock without
reporting an error.

The provider is chosen from the environment:

| Variable | Effect |
|---|---|
| `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` | Selects the TypeSafe route when present |
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | Selects the OpenRouter route when present and no TypeSafe key is set |
| `JEV_PROVIDER` | `mock`, `live`, or `openrouter` — overrides the heuristic above |
| `TYPESAFE_MODEL` / `OPENROUTER_MODEL` | Model id for the selected route |
| `TYPESAFE_BASE_URL` / `OPENROUTER_BASE_URL` | API root for the selected route |

With neither key it stays on the offline mock. Unlike the plugin, the MCP server
resolves its credential once at startup, so a missing key with
`JEV_PROVIDER=live` is a startup error rather than a per-call surprise.
